newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ENGLISH SLAM UEFA'S WORLD CUP SUPPORT FOR GERMANY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ENGLISH SLAM UEFA'S WORLD CUP SUPPORT FOR GERMANY.

text.p: The English Football Association (F.A.) lashed out on Saturday after discovering UEFA has backed Germany's proposed bid to host the 2006 World Cup finals ahead of England's.
The F.A. told a hastily arranged news conference at its London headquarters that UEFA's decision was "astonishing" "undemocratic" and "entirely unacceptable".
Spokesman David Davies said they had received an unexpected fax from European soccer's governing body UEFA on Friday.

In the fax, copies of which were made available to reporters, UEFA revealed that its executive committee which met in Lisbon this week was concerned that England and Germany were planning rival bids for the 2006 tournament.
"In this context the committee recalled that it had already committed itself to supporting the candidature of the Football Association of Germany as organiser of the World Cup in 2006," the fax read.
Davies told reporters: "It made no reference as to when or where this decision had been taken. At this stage there is no evidence that it was ever recorded publicly.
"The final decision as to who stages the World Cup of 2006 is scheduled to be taken in June of the year 2000 by FIFA, football's world governing body," Davies said. "It is not a decision for UEFA."
"Is it correct that three and a bit years before a decision on the finals is to be formally announced, one of the bids is not to be considered?" he asked.
He said the F.A. had no alternative but to see the fax as "evidence of an attempt at a very early stage to prevent England's bid from receiving proper consideration."
"The attempt will not succeed," he vowed, adding that he had received messages of support from Britain's prime minister John Major and the leader of the opposition Labour Party Tony Blair.
F.A. chief executive Graham Kelly said he had no idea when UEFA decided to back the Germans or if it had ever made the decision known.
"We haven't been able to find any minutes, we haven't been able to find any published material," he said.
"It's not a dispute between England and Germany. We have stressed that we want both bids to be considered fairly, openly and democratically."
"But we cannot sit back and allow this sort of thing to happen to English football. We have a duty to the game in England."

The row will come as a serious embarrassment to world soccer body FIFA, which is keen to ensure the bid for the 2006 tournament runs smoothly after the squabbling that marred the contest for the 2002 tournament, which was awarded jointly to bitter regional rivals Japan and South Korea.
After successfully staging the European championships last year, English officials feel their World Cup claims for 2006 are particularly strong.
They also point out England has not hosted soccer's premier tournament since 1966, whereas Germany held the tournament in 1974.
